claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi can be prepared as a single-phase FCC solid solution by high-temperature homogenization.
The proposed initial CoCrFeMnNi state has a uniform elemental distribution and no significant grain-boundary segregation.
Extended high-temperature annealing minimizes nanoscale chemical clustering in CoCrFeMnNi.
Rapid quenching promotes nanoscale chemical heterogeneity and nanocluster formation in CoCrFeMnNi.
Controlled thermal-gradient processing promotes nanoscale chemical heterogeneity and nanocluster formation in CoCrFeMnNi.
Intramatrix compositional nanoclusters locally impede dislocation mobility.
Compositional nanoclusters create local stress concentrations and weak links for crack initiation.
Nanocluster-driven brittleness can occur independently of conventional grain-boundary segregation or intermetallic precipitation.
Nanoscale chemical heterogeneity disrupts uniform plastic deformation.
Nanoclusters reduce the alloy's ability to redistribute stress during deformation.
Nanoclusters preferentially nucleate brittle cracks within the matrix.
Enhanced nanoscale heterogeneity lowers the ductile-to-brittle transition threshold relative to a homogenized alloy.
Heterogeneous samples will show an earlier onset of brittle fracture than homogenized samples under identical service conditions.
Heterogeneous samples will have lower ductility and toughness than homogenized samples.
Nanoclusters will spatially correlate with localized crack-initiation sites.
The homogenized baseline will retain superior ductility and toughness because it has less local clustering.
Grain-boundary segregation and nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, and Mn at elevated temperature can cause grain-boundary decohesion in CoCrFeMnNi.
Grain-boundary second-phase precipitation can create stress and strain concentrations because particle and matrix deformation are incompatible.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says heterogeneity lowers the ductile-to-brittle transition threshold, which conventionally implies improved low-temperature toughness, while the predicted outcome says it causes an earlier onset of brittle fracture. The intended threshold direction is therefore internally ambiguous or reversed.
